- Avoid over-optimism in early forecast periods; model tends to overshoot after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is neutral or flat.
- When sentiment remains zero (or unchanged), model should not assume momentum; mean reversion is likely, and forecasts should be anchored to recent 7–14 day averages.
- If true outcome shows sharp downward correction after a forecast peak, reduce forecast slope for next 3–5 days; avoid “overcorrection” after spikes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; adjust downward by 2–5% for days 25–30 if sentiment remains flat.
- If true outcome diverges from forecast by >5% in first 5 days, flag for re-calibration; sentiment history should be used to trigger early correction if no news events.
- When sentiment is zero, model should not assume upward trend; use 14-day moving average as baseline for forecasting, not 30-day trend.
- Avoid forecasting upward when recent 7-day average is below 70; model tends to ignore support levels when sentiment is neutral.
